I see this commonly used for voaters ;). What does it mean to be meta?

(of a creative work) referring to itself or to the conventions of its genre; self-referential.

On the context of voat and its subverse, it is to post a topic/discussion about what is happening on that subverse/entirety of voat.

An example is a thread discussing what the subscribers/moderators of a subverse, say v/mechanicalkeyboards, on weather they need to refer to the general v/keyboards instead as the community is still relatively small. It is a post that belongs to that subverse, but the topic is not directed at 'mechanical keyboards'. Some subverse do make an entire new subverse for meta post like v/metaAnime.

What is your favorite Band/Artist, and what is it about them that makes them your favorite?

Dream Theater; I'm not musically trained, so I can't really comment on their technical skills, but I just love the diversity of music they have. Even in their, ah hem, respectable age, they're still kicking musical ass. Their music ages well.
Iron Maiden. Mainly the riffs and lyrics, oh and those bass lines!

Instumental artist would have to be Sungha Jung. He's a Korean guitarist. As a musician whose guitar broke (can't afford to get it fixed or get a new one), it's lovely to have something to listen to, whatever the mood.

A singer would have to be Gabrielle Aplin, simply for her voice. It's great.

Tool. I'll probably get shit on for this but I don't care. It's the only music that truly makes me feel something amazing. I can interpret much of it into things that I can relate to. I think it's poeticism at its finest. Gives me the heebie jeebies
Queen. Reminds me of riding in the truck with my brothers and dad on the way to school.

The Used. I really enjoyed their earlier stuff during my emo phase, and now that I'm growing out of it, their sound has grown up a bit too. I think their music is going to keep evolving really nicely as the years go on.

My favorite band is Van Halen. I like how everyone in the band is a good performer and is really good at their instrument(s). I also like how they have a good sound and don't really have many serious songs (Right Now is the only one I can think of at the moment). Eddie's solos are also fun to listen to and play.
Alt-J. I love that no matter how often I listen to their music, I can always discover something new in their songs.
Odesza. I just love their sound so much

Between the Buried and Me. They change genres around so much while still remaining an overall progressive metal sound. Their music never gets old because they are constantly changing their style and atmosphere. They are the only band that I like every single song from. I don't think I can say that about any other band.
GWAR. Costumes, live show, lyrics... They have it all! Fuck you, Brockie!

Mac Demarco. Not only is his music lighthearted and enjoyable, but the dudes a straight goof. He put his address at the end of his newest album that just leaked so people could come hang for a bit. Wish I could meet him myself, he seems like like a real chill guy.
I saw him live, and during the show, my friend's brother invited him to a party. He went.

Koji Kondo, best known for his work on Nintendo games. He doesn't get as much attention as Miyamoto or Sakurai, but I'd argue his music is just as integral to a quality title. Even if you're not familiar with his name, you're almost definitely familiar with his work.

Between the Buried and Me. They make amazing concept albums and are the most diverse band I've ever listened to. It's hard to staple them to a genre but I think they're Progressive Metal. You should check them out but they do scream.

AC/DC, They always lift my spirits. I know music, played a few shows myself back in the day and enjoy these guys because their songs are easy to tap your foot to and you always know what you'll get from them. They do not try to fit in, change or cater for other genres, they just rock.
They are the best rock and roll band of all time in my opinion. That's all they play. Just gritty, dirty rock. I love 'em.
Papa Roach. They put on one helluva show. So much stage presence, and energy. I've seen them 5 times and they never fail.

Beck. He has such a wide variety of sounds and he does them all so well. He's been one of my favorites since I was a kid and I've only grown to appreciate his work more over the years. He's friggin awesome live, too!

classical music...i have to say beethoven..besides the great music he left us...i love how he overcame what he did...to become one of the single most important figures in music.(imo) also good ol joe strummer! so much to say....and he inteneded to say it...

Toss up between either Led Zeppelin or Blue Oyster Cult. Both are bands I can always listen too and their music always engages me. Both had excellent guitar players, and in the case of Led Zeppelin and extremely good rhythm section between John Bonham and John Paul Jones.

Faith No More. They're unique and they've had a huge influence on the bands that followed them. Patton's vocals are unparalleled, they still whip crowds into a frenzy when they play, and the guys are all into their fifties now (save Patton). FNM was the core of the soundtrack to my teenage years.

Ozzy. The man ought to have died a thousand times over, and yet he's still around. The first time I heard The Ultimate Sin playing on my sister's record player, I was forever changed. He's certainly not the best out there, but something about his music speaks to me and that means a lot, at least in my humble opinion.

King Crimson. They've managed to exist from the late 60s to the present day and never once have they stopped being inventive and ahead of the times. Never once have they become a shadow of their former self. I honestly can't think of any other band that has managed to consistently innovate and change their formula for 50-ish years. Usually when classic rock bands survive until the present day, they become a sort of "greatest hits"/"remember how great we were" kind of band.

I, like the vast majority of you, have come here from Reddit. After six years. Six years of getting my daily fix of news, science, memes, politics, technology and gaming updates and discussion . The current direction of Reddit, we can all agree, is fucked. The larger news sites (including The Verge) are painting a picture that leaving Reddit as it was is cowardly and irresponsible. That having a self-policing network of communities online has lead to a cesspit of child porn and hate speech. I was never exposed to any of that on the site. I didn't see this stuff cause I didn't go looking for it. It didn't jump out from a pop up at me while I was browsing r/WorldNews or /EDC. I watched with some trepidation after the closing of r/FPH and the like. I jumped ship after the latest AMAgate shitstorm. I'm seeing a media company being born out of the ashes of a really cool forum site and it's sad. It's also doomed to fail.

The reason Reddit is censoring isn't because it feels some social responsibility to shut down offensive communities. It's just economics. It is chasing corporate dollars. It is struggling to find a way to convert all that traffic and userbase into bucks. And it can't sell well while places like r/Coontown still exist to be written about in pieces by Slate. The Snowden revelations were able to be published, discussed and disseminated on the broader subs of Reddit because of the core nature of what Reddit was. Of course it was the news organisations who brought the story out into the public but Reddit was instrumental in spreading the few outlets that stood up to the NSA and US Gov who published against their will. The admins didn't used to take responsibility for content on Reddit. That's now starting to happen, which is why they're actively shutting down subs. When the next Snowden type event happens, Reddit has put itself in a position where it can far more easily be subjected to take down demands from the US Gov and other powerful political or corporate bodies.

I have high hopes for Voat. The hypocritical knots Reddit's founders are currently tying themselves in about free speech and the original intentions for the site do make me wonder what Voat will turn into eventually. I think all organisations of people, when they get big enough, are doomed to go the way of Reddit. But for now, I'm optimistic for this site and what it can stand for. edit: formatting
